definitions.explanation: To prepare tea, especially matcha, by whisking the powdered tea with hot water using a bamboo whisk. A term associated with tea ceremony and traditional tea preparation.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}がお{茶|ちゃ}を{点|た}ててくださった。
examples.english: The teacher made tea for us.

examples.japanese: {茶道|さどう}の{稽古|けいこ}で{初|はじ}めて{自分|じぶん}でお{茶|ちゃ}を{点|た}てたが、{泡|あわ}がうまく{立|た}たなかった。
examples.english: I made tea by myself for the first time in tea ceremony practice, but I couldn't get a good froth.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive ({他動詞|たどうし}). No intransitive pair.

USAGE:
This verb is specific to preparing tea, especially {抹茶|まっちゃ}. It is not used for brewing other beverages. For making regular tea ({煎茶|せんちゃ} etc.), use {入|い}れる or {淹|い}れる instead.

The polite form お{茶|ちゃ}を{点|た}てる is very common, reflecting the formality associated with {茶道|さどう} (tea ceremony).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {抹茶|まっちゃ}を{点|た}てる: to make matcha
- お{茶|ちゃ}を{点|た}てる: to make tea (polite)
- {薄茶|うすちゃ}を{点|た}てる: to make thin tea
- {濃茶|こいちゃ}を{点|た}てる: to make thick tea
